classification.difficultyReason: Reads successive graph values and calculates interval distances, then distinguishes rising or falling distance from increasing or decreasing speed and explains speed through steepness magnitude.

content.prompt: Each graph below is part of a distance–time graph.

spec.description: Increasing curve with decreasing steepness, square grid, positive axis arrows and a broken distance axis below 200 m.
spec.mathematics: Readings at t=0,1,2,3,4 s are approximately 200,225,233,238,240 m. No equation is supplied; the curve is a qualitative interpolation through graph readings.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is always visible; interval calculations are answers.

spec.description: Decreasing curve becoming less steep, square grid, positive axis arrows and a broken distance axis below 130 m.
spec.mathematics: Readings at t=0,1,2,3,4 s are approximately 180,160,150,145,142 m. No equation is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is always visible; interval calculations are answers.

spec.description: Decreasing curve becoming steeper, square grid, positive axis arrows and a broken distance axis below 200 m.
spec.mathematics: Readings at t=0,1,2,3,4 s are approximately 260,255,245,230,210 m. No equation is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is always visible; interval calculations are answers.

spec.description: Increasing curve becoming steeper, square grid, positive axis arrows and a broken distance axis below 150 m.
spec.mathematics: Readings at t=0,1,2,3,4 s are approximately 150,152,157,165,183 m. No equation is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is always visible; interval calculations are answers.

children.label: v
children.prompt: Describe how distance is changing over this four second period, using the phrase “increasing/decreasing at an increasing/decreasing rate”.

answer.short: Distance increases at a decreasing rate.
answer.worked: Distance increases at a decreasing rate: the curve rises but becomes less steep.

answer.short: Distance decreases at a decreasing rate.
answer.worked: Distance decreases at a decreasing rate: the curve falls but becomes less steep.

answer.short: Distance decreases at an increasing rate.
answer.worked: Distance decreases at an increasing rate: the curve falls and becomes steeper.

answer.short: Distance increases at an increasing rate.
answer.worked: Distance increases at an increasing rate: the curve rises and becomes steeper.

children.label: vi
children.prompt: How does the steepness of a line relate to how quickly distance is changing?

answer.short: The steeper the curve, the faster distance changes and the greater the speed.
answer.worked: The steeper the curve at a point, the more quickly distance changes at that time, so the speed is greater. This applies whether distance is increasing or decreasing.
